answer: Place each identity in a 12-epoch probation behind a 140-unit refundable bond. Every epoch it completes one random task and receives three attestations from peers with no shared recent contacts; copied wording, reused proofs, or synchronized timing freezes the bond for three epochs. The ledger checks signatures, task uniqueness, peer independence, and time windows. Each sybil alias therefore locks 140 units and repeats twelve rounds, while an island of correlated traces exposes the cluster; lantern assignments vary the work, and beacon timestamps make coordinated imitation costly.
